extracted.intended_audience: solo inventors, small businesses, and non-profits in Pennsylvania seeking pro bono patent assistance (and volunteer patent practitioners)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and program requirements for eligibility, intake, and participation in Penn State Dickinson Law's Patent Pro Bono Program, including applicant financial/residency limits, invention standards (patent eligibility, reduction to practice, disclosure timing), required training and prior-art search, and volunteer guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program admission and placement discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must read all program information and meet the published requirements. Placement with a volunteer patent practitioner is at the sole discretion of the program administrator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You will not be admitted if you do not meet requirements. Placement is discretionary; program staff review applications and may send follow-up questions. Intake appointment must be attended in person.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant conduct expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must be prepared, courteous, and respectful to LaunchBox staff, Penn State Law students or staff, and volunteer patent practitioners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to be prepared, courteous, and respectful will result in expulsion from the program and denial of future services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solo inventor — number of inventors
rubrics_metrics.description: To qualify as a Solo Inventor there must be exactly 1 known inventor for the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solo inventor — residency
rubrics_metrics.description: Solo inventor must reside in Pennsylvania.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solo inventor — income threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Solo inventor's total household income must be less than 400% of the federal poverty guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See aspe.hhs.gov for federal poverty guideline values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solo inventor — ownership interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Solo inventor must not be under an obligation to assign (sell or give ownership of) the patent rights to a third party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solo inventor — prior patent filings limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Solo inventor must not have filed 4 or more patent applications with the United States Patent & Trademark Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-profit — number of inventors
rubrics_metrics.description: For non-profit applicants there must be no more than 4 known inventors of the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-profit — inventor assignment to organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Each inventor must agree to assign his/her rights to the non-profit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-profit — individual inventor residency
rubrics_metrics.description: Each inventor listed must reside in Pennsylvania.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-profit — individual inventor income
rubrics_metrics.description: Each inventor must have a total household income of less than 400% of the federal poverty guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-profit — individual prior patent filings limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Each inventor must not have filed 4 or more patent applications with the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-profit — type exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: The non-profit must not be a research institution or an institution of higher learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-profit — corporate/residency and tax status
rubrics_metrics.description: The non-profit must be a domestic corporation established in Pennsylvania with 501(c)(3) status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-profit — previous year budget cap
rubrics_metrics.description: The non-profit must have had a budget of less than $175,000 in the previous calendar year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-profit — projected year budget cap
rubrics_metrics.description: The non-profit must have a budget of less than $175,000 in the current calendar year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-profit — ownership interest
rubrics_metrics.description: The non-profit must not be under an obligation to assign (sell or give ownership of) the patent rights to a third party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small business / inventor group — number of inventors
rubrics_metrics.description: For a small business or inventor group there must be no more than 4 known inventors for the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small business — inventor assignment to business
rubrics_metrics.description: Each inventor must agree to assign his/her rights to the business.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small business — individual inventor residency
rubrics_metrics.description: Each inventor must reside in Pennsylvania.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small business — individual inventor income
rubrics_metrics.description: Each inventor must have a total household income of less than 400% of the federal poverty guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small business — individual prior patent filings limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Each inventor must not have filed 4 or more patent applications with the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small business — previous year gross income cap
rubrics_metrics.description: If the business was operating in the preceding calendar year, it must have had total gross income of less than $150,000.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small business — projected year gross income cap
rubrics_metrics.description: The business must expect total gross income of less than $150,000 in the current calendar year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small business — ownership interest
rubrics_metrics.description: The business must not be under an obligation to assign (sell or give ownership of) the patent rights to a third party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invention — patent eligibility requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The invention must be of a patent-eligible type: a process, machine, manufacture, composition of matter, a new and useful improvement thereof, an ornamental design for an article of manufacture, or an asexually reproduced plant (with statutory exceptions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These categories are the kinds of inventions that qualify for assistance by the Patent Pro Bono Program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invention — patent-ineligible subject matter (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some inventions do not qualify: products of nature, abstract ideas, laws of nature, natural phenomena, certain business methods, and perpetual-motion/cold-fusion devices; other examples provided include methods of detecting credit-card fraud, certain investment instruments, antenatal screening methods, cloned mammals (the mammal itself), and certain lipid compositions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page lists specific examples to illustrate ineligible subjects. If unsure, applicants are directed to contact their local LaunchBox or the program site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invention — other non-patent-eligible items
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-patent items such as brands, business names, artwork, trademarks, t-shirt designs, rules of playing a game, and recipes do not qualify for assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If seeking assistance for non-patent topics, applicants should contact LaunchBox resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction to practice requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Invention must be 'reduced to practice' — either a working prototype or a written description sufficiently detailed that a person of ordinary skill in the relevant field could make and use the invention without outside assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A reduction to practice assures a definite and permanent manifestation of an invention; general goals or research plans do not qualify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure timing — program limit (10 months)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventors who publicly disclosed the invention more than 10 months prior to program submission cannot be placed with a pro bono attorney through the program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: U.S. law gives one year from first disclosure to file; the program requires at least 2 months for attorneys to prepare and file, so disclosures older than 10 months make placement ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good-faith belief in novelty and non-obviousness
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventor must have a good-faith belief that they were first to invent/discover the invention, that it has not been patented/described/in public use/on sale by another, and that a person having ordinary skill in the art would not know how to make and use the invention from a simple combination of prior art references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required patent training
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to intake or placement, each inventor must participate in an approved patent training seminar or demonstrate they have been a named inventor on another patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All inventors to be listed must either already be listed on another patent/pending application, attend an approved training seminar, or complete the USPTO's online patent training module and submit the completion certificate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required prior art search (mandatory)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventors must conduct a prior art search and find at least 3 relevant prior art references prior to scheduling an intake meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is mandatory; the program will not accept 'there is nothing like my invention' as an appropriate response. You should be able to identify at least one similarity and one difference between a reference and your invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior art — what counts and search resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior art includes prior patents (U.S. or foreign), published articles, public demonstrations, and other public disclosures (including products for sale anywhere in the world).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended search resources: USPTO PatFT & AppFT, European Patent Office (Espacenet), Google Patents, paid services, and product searches on retail sites; EPO/foreign patents count because the USPTO considers global prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior art search example and expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: A well-done search should reveal similar inventions and educate the inventor on the current state of the field; you are asked to find similar inventions, not necessarily an exact match.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: umbrella-with-ground-illumination inventor could cite a traditional umbrella, a flashlight, and a light sensor as three relevant references—none individually disclose all elements but are valid references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercial search results requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Commercial prior art searches are permitted but results must be less than 3 months old and you must provide a copy of the contract with the search company.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The contract is required so the program can ensure you have not disclosed the invention or assigned patent rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-application checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: Before applying, applicants must have read/completed prior steps, have name and email of each inventor, collect financial info for each inventor (and business/non-profit if applicable), basic invention info, and information on previous patents/applications filed by each inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete the Solo Inventor or Small Business/Non-Profit application depending on number of inventors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Which application to use
rubrics_metrics.description: If only one inventor will be listed, use the Solo Inventor Application; if two or more inventors will be listed, use the Small Business/Non-Profit Application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application review and intake process
rubrics_metrics.description: After submitting an application, staff will review answers, contact applicants within a reasonable period, send follow-up questions if qualified, and schedule an in-person intake appointment once questions are answered to staff satisfaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not qualified, the program will inform the applicant of the reason and provide resources on filing pro se or acquiring assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expected response time and review delays
rubrics_metrics.description: The program attempts to contact applicants within 1 week, but application reviews may take longer during certain periods (mid-December to mid-January; mid-March; late April–early May; mid-May–mid-June; early–late August; mid–late October).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These periods coincide with law school semester changes, staffing transitions, events, or holidays; applicants should exercise patience if applying during these windows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Volunteer participation — malpractice insurance
rubrics_metrics.description: The program does not provide malpractice insurance for volunteer attorneys.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Volunteers should consult their own malpractice carrier about specifics for particular cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Volunteer pairing criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Volunteer patent attorneys are matched with inventors based on the field of the invention and the volunteer's expertise or knowledge of that field, while considering conflicts issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Volunteer responsibilities and scope of services
rubrics_metrics.description: Scope of services is flexible to accommodate both volunteer attorney and inventor needs; an engagement letter is strongly recommended to define scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In general, services focus on preparation, filing, and prosecution of a patent application before the USPTO. Volunteers should define expectations in an engagement letter.
